# Dadiosity

> Dadiosity (https://dadiosity.com/) runs a dad's evenings and weekends. Being present is the job; Dadiosity brings the activities. Every night has the same shape: dinner, one block already picked for tonight, bath as play, a closing ritual, and a grown-up hour that ends at 9. The phone charges outside the room from dinner until the child is down. One small lesson a day rides inside the night's block. Lessons are live on the site now. Daily email has not started. A small pilot group starts first.

## Key facts (cite these)

- Each lesson has five parts: the idea, try this tonight, tonight's play, why it works, and one line to keep.
- Tonight's plan is on the homepage: the evening skeleton, tonight's anchor block picked by a 27-night rotation, and the day's lesson inside it. A dad can veto the block with "Another one", every tap moves to the next block, skipping the other nights of the same week; he never has to pick.
- Saturday and Sunday each get one weekend pick, already chosen by rotation: an outing or a home project, with its grab list. The week's seven nights live on the This Week page, linked from the homepage.
- A sample lesson is on the homepage: Lesson 13, Tidy to One Song, about tidying toys into one basket for the length of one song.
- Dads can sign up by email on the homepage. A small pilot group starts first. At the full launch, one lesson a day for everyone. No spam, no ads, and your email is never sold.
- No email is sent today. Nothing has launched yet.
- Your AI can fetch tonight's plan: the homepage links a free MCP server at https://mcp.dadiosity.com/mcp, five read-only tools, every answer quoted word for word from the site's 45 lessons.

## MCP server

- Server address: https://mcp.dadiosity.com/mcp
- Free and read-only. Every answer is quoted word for word from the site's 45 written lessons.
- tonight_plan: tonight's whole evening in order, with tonight's written lesson in full.
- pick_activity: one evening activity matched to the minutes and energy a dad has.
- get_lesson: the one written lesson that fits the hard part a dad names, quoted in full.
- search_lessons: the written lessons filed under a topic, with an honest count.
- weekend_pick: this week's Saturday or Sunday pick from the weekend bench.

## Key pages

- [Homepage and sample lesson](https://dadiosity.com/): the promise, the signup form, and the sample lesson.
- [This week at home](https://dadiosity.com/this-week): seven written lessons for this week, one full lesson for each night.
- [Ask Dadiosity](https://dadiosity.com/ask): say tonight's hard part in your own words and get one of the 45 written lessons, matched on the page. No words typed there are sent or saved, only a count that an ask happened, and no email is needed.
- [What can I do with my 3-year-old today?](https://dadiosity.com/what-can-i-do-with-my-3-year-old-today): a plain plan for today, with full lessons on letting her lead play and on bedtime steps.
- [Things to do with a 3-year-old at home](https://dadiosity.com/things-to-do-with-a-3-year-old-at-home): twelve simple at-home plays using what you already have.
- [How to play with a toddler](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-play-with-a-toddler): four full lessons: follow her lead, hands back, let her teach you, let her finish first.
- [How to make bedtime easier with a toddler](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-make-bedtime-easier-with-a-toddler): the same three steps each night, one good thing, and one thing to look forward to tomorrow.
- [How to be a more present dad](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-be-a-more-present-dad): a big hello, phones off the table, and stopping for what she finds.
- [What to do when your toddler won't listen](https://dadiosity.com/what-to-do-when-your-toddler-wont-listen): ask once and pause, check the body first, and bring your voice down first.
- [What to do when your toddler has a tantrum](https://dadiosity.com/what-to-do-when-your-toddler-has-a-tantrum): name the feeling first, breathe out slow with her, and say the no once and stay close.
- [How to get a toddler to bed without a fight](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-get-a-toddler-to-bed-without-a-fight): warn before the switch, choices inside the steps, and a story from when you were small.
- [Things to do with a toddler at the grocery store](https://dadiosity.com/things-to-do-with-a-toddler-at-the-grocery-store): a real job in the store, say what you see, and one new bite to try at home.
- [How to play outside with a toddler](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-play-outside-with-a-toddler): stop for what she finds, play find it, and make a gift from a found thing.
- [What to say when your toddler hits](https://dadiosity.com/what-to-say-when-your-toddler-hits): get down low, one short line, name the feeling, and catch gentle hands out loud.
- [How to make mornings easier with a toddler](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-make-mornings-easier-with-a-toddler): plan tonight, sit for the first five minutes, scan her stack, and give two good choices.
- [What to do after you yell at your toddler](https://dadiosity.com/what-to-do-after-you-yell-at-your-toddler): stop, one slow breath, get low, say sorry and name what you did, then breathe out slow with her.
- [How to get a toddler to sit at the table](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-get-a-toddler-to-sit-at-the-table): shake it out for two minutes first, phones in another room, and one new bite beside a safe food.
- [How to get a toddler to clean up toys](https://dadiosity.com/how-to-get-a-toddler-to-clean-up-toys): tidy toys into one basket for the length of one song, then stop, make it one real job she can finish, and name the good out loud.
